summary: Edinburgh Law School offers three master's awards for 2027–28: one scholarship covering the full tuition fee of the LLM in European and Transnational Law, one of £10,000 for the LLM in Comparative Private Law, and three Tercentenary Awards of £5,000 for any taught LLM or MSc. Apply for the programme, then send the scholarship form by 30 April 2027.
meta_description: Edinburgh Law School: full tuition for the European and Transnational Law LLM, £10,000 for Comparative Private Law, three £5,000 awards. Apply by 30 April 2027.
covers: LLM European and Transnational Law Scholarship: the full tuition fee, at the home or international rate, for one student.
LLM Comparative Private Law Scholarship: £10,000 off tuition for one student.
Tercentenary Awards for Excellence: three awards of £5,000 off tuition for any taught LLM or MSc, online programmes included.
eligibility: Accepted for a taught LLM or MSc at Edinburgh Law School starting in 2027–28, and firmly accepted or intending to accept the offer.
For the two named awards, an application to that specific full-time LLM.
Priority goes to applicants who have not studied at master's level before. Awards are on academic merit and a personal statement.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the LLM or MSc and mention the scholarship in your application.
Complete Edinburgh Law School's scholarship application form and email it to pg.law.enquiries@ed.ac.uk by 30 April 2027.
Edinburgh tells applicants the outcome by the end of June 2027.
watch_out: All three awards pay tuition only; living costs are yours.
You need an offer before the scholarship deadline, so apply for the programme early.
Each award is for one or three people, so apply for other funding too.
costs: Fully or partly covered, by award
documents: An application for a taught LLM or MSc at Edinburgh Law School
The Law School scholarship application form, including a personal statement
